title: Adaptive presubmit minimizer and release-probe shim
author: Sana Kapoor
description:
Motivation: our presubmit lane has grown noisy and slow as we added more language-specific linters and heavy integration tests. This PR introduces an adaptive presubmit minimizer (aka 'sieve') that computes a minimal set of checks required for a given change based on file fingerprints and a cheap dependency-stability probe. It also adds a small release-probe shim used by staged release automation to perform a lightweight smoke validation before triggering the full release pipeline.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces presubmit fingerprinting: a checksum-based classifier that maps changed paths to the minimal lint/test shards required. Fingerprints are cached in an indexed artifact in the repo CI cache.
- Adds a dependency-stability probe that runs a fast npm/pip install with a dry-run verification to detect transitive resolution changes before running full dependency-heavy checks.
- Implements selective toolchain microimages for fast presubmit lanes (tiny container images with only the necessary runtime toolchain for the detected shards).
- Adds a release-probe shim that runs a deterministic subset of end-to-end smoke flows (auth handshake, health endpoints, simple inference call) against the release candidate in a staging namespace. The shim can be run on-demand or automatically by the release orchestrator.
- Provides telemetry hooks to Redwood Console for presubmit latency and the probe success rate so SRE and platform teams can tune thresholds.

Why this approach: previous attempts at broad presubmit pruning were brittle (overfitting to sparse path globs) and caused missed failures. Fingerprinting + a fast dep-stability probe gives high precision while keeping false negatives low. Microimages reduce presubmit setup time without changing developer-facing CI semantics. The release-probe shim addresses a common gap where releases went green in CI but failed quick sanity checks in staging.

Checklist included in PR description: 
- [x] Add presubmit fingerprint generator + serializer
- [x] Integrate probe runner into presubmit coordinator
- [x] Provide microimage Dockerfiles and build manifest
- [x] Add feature flag (ci.presubmit.minimizer.enabled) for staged rollout
- [x] Add telemetry counters and Grafana dashboard stub
- [x] Unit tests for fingerprint invariant and probe failure handling
- [x] End-to-end smoke test for release-probe shim

Compatibility and rollout plan: feature gated via a repo-level flag (default off). We will enable the minimizer for 10% of PRs in the fastpath lane for one week, monitor presubmit latency, probe false positive/negative signals, and then ramp to 50% and 100% if metrics look healthy. The release-probe shim is opt-in for release automation and will be added to the canary release stage for the first 2 releases.

Testing and CI notes: initial CI run showed a lint shard flake due to an ESLint rule mismatch; I updated the ruleset in the microimage bootstrap and retriggered. Full CI passed on the second run (unit + shard smoke + release-probe smoke). See CI timeline below in review conversation.

Files changed (high level): changed presubmit coordinator, added fingerprint generator, probe runner, microimage Dockerfiles, small release automation hook, Grafana dashboard JSON stub, and associated tests.

Impact: reduces average presubmit latency in fastpath by ~38% in internal benchmarks for typical frontend and sdk PRs. Expected to cut CI run compute units for presubmit by ~22% after ramp. Improves early detection of dependency resolution regressions for node/python tooling.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4821: add caching sharding to fingerprint index and rotate stale entries
- ENG-4890: wire probe results into rollback policies for release orchestrator

Notes for reviewers: the PR intentionally keeps the minimizer behind a feature flag and does not change existing lint/test definitions. Look specifically at the fingerprint collision guard logic (fingerprint_guard_test.js) and the probe time budget heuristics in probe-runner.go.

release_notes:
- Add adaptive presubmit minimizer: fingerprints map changed files to minimal presubmit shards
- Introduce dependency-stability probe to catch transitive resolution changes early
- Add small release-probe shim for deterministic pre-release smoke checks
- Provide selective microimages to speed up presubmit setup
- Feature gated; rollout plan and metrics included
notes_for_ops: Feature flag ci.presubmit.minimizer.enabled defaults to false. To enable: update ci/feature-flags.yaml and restart ci-coordinator. Microimages are published to internal registry at ghcr.redwood/infer/microimage-<lang>:<semver>. Release-probe requires staging namespace with health endpoints exposed and service account with minimal read permissions.
testing_summary: Unit tests: fingerprint invariants and probe failure handling. Integration: microimage bootstrap and selected shard runs on a sample repo. Release-probe smoke validated against staging canary. CI initially had one lint failure, fixed and rerun. All checks green on final run.
risk_assessment: Low. Changes are behind a feature flag and fall back to existing behavior on fingerprint collisions or probe failures. Microimages are optional and do not replace full images until ramped. The release-probe runs a non-destructive smoke and will not gate a release unless explicitly enabled.
operational_playbook: If presubmit minimizer causes missed checks: disable ci.presubmit.minimizer.enabled and run presubmit coordinator in audit mode (ENV CI_COORD_AUDIT=true) to produce a diagnostic log of fingerprint decisions. For probe failures, consult probe-runner logs (tools/ci/probe) and validate with a one-off dry-run (--dry-run) to reproduce.
